29:     The second term carries a plus: with a minus the result is not a group
30:     operation (``0 (+) y`` would be ``-y``) and every map built on it, the

32:     names.

36:     xy = (x * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True)

Per training forward there are exactly three distinct all_reduces (one per residual level), `distributed.all_reduce(used, ...)` at model/layers.py:165-166; per step, after `optimizer.step()`, exactly six, `dist.all_reduce(tangent_sum/weight_sum, SUM)` at train_rqvae.py:455-457, iterated over `raw_module.frechet_step_sums()` which returns one entry per level because every level gets `frechet` (config `frechet_codebook=True`) and every level's `_last` is filled by the same forward at model/layers.py:157; per epoch two, `all_reduce(local_loss/local_recon)` at train_rqvae.py:468-470; barriers at train_rqvae.py:420 and 517; the one-off `dist.broadcast` of the KMeans centres at model/layers.py:191-192 and of the fitted codebook at train_rqvae.py:418-419. All of these sit in control flow that depends only on `epoch`, `world_size` and the constant layer count, never on rank, so the order and count match on every rank. The rank-0-only evaluation/export pass is the only asymmetric branch: it is fenced on both sides by `_skip_ddp_reduce = True/False` set on ALL ranks (train_rqvae.py:486-487 and 514-515, and 544-545 for the export), so the three `used` all_reduces of the forward are skipped on rank 0 and no rank is inside a collective the others do not enter; the others simply wait at `dist.barrier()` (train_rqvae.py:517, 566). `find_unused_parameters=False` is safe: `VQLayer.__init__` calls `self.embed.weight.requires_grad_(False)` at model/layers.py:84 before `DDP(...)` is constructed at train_rqvae.py:346-351, so the manually written codebook is never registered with the reducer (no "Expected to have finished reduction in the prior iteration" on step 2), while encoder and decoder both receive gradient — the decoder through `reconstructed = self.decoder(quantized)` and the encoder through the straight-through `x_q = x + (x_q - x).detach()` at model/layers.py:182 plus the curved commitment at model/layers.py:176-177. I also checked that the eval branch cannot poison the next step's sums: the all-items `get_indices` at train_rqvae.py:492-496 overwrites `_last` on rank 0 only, but `frechet_step_sums()` is always read after a fresh training forward, which rewrites `_last` on every rank.

CHECK: shared state: codebook, cache and counters across ranks
CHECK VERDICT: NEEDS_FIX
EXERCISED PATH: model/layers.py:188-203 (`init_codebook`), model/frechet_poincare.py:88-98 (`poincare_distance`), train_rqvae.py:405-420 (the codebook-initialisation broadcast) | The equality half of this check is correct: the KMeans start is produced on every rank over the same `train_embeddings` (train_rqvae.py:325-330), each level's centres are broadcast inside `VQLayer.init_codebook` (model/layers.py:191-192), the trainer broadcasts every level's fitted codebook again after the DDP wrapper exists (train_rqvae.py:418-419) and then barriers, and thereafter every slot move is computed from the cross-rank reduced `(tangent_sum, weight_sum)` and applied identically on every rank (train_rqvae.py:451-459 -> model/model.py:65-80), so the manual `.data.copy_` write at model/model.py:80 cannot leave the ranks holding different SIDs. The one-off `item_weights` table is built from the same train parquet on every rank and bound before DDP is built (train_rqvae.py:335-339), so `broadcast_buffers=False` is harmless. The defect below is in what is put into that shared state, not in whether the ranks agree.

FINDING SEVERITY: blocking
FINDING LOCATION: model/layers.py:198-201 (with model/frechet_poincare.py:88-98, 143-151)
FINDING DETAIL: The level-2/level-3 codebook initialisation applies the Poincare distance to a point that is not in the ball. `VQLayer.init_codebook` receives `x` = the residual handed in from the previous level, which at level 1 is the raw encoder output in R^d and at levels 2-3 is a tangent residual `x - log_0(code)`. It then does `embed_ind = torch.argmin(self.frechet.distances(x, self.get_code_embs()), dim=-1)` where `distances` (curvature on) evaluates `poincare_distance(x.unsqueeze(1), codebook.unsqueeze(0))`, i.e. it treats that unbounded tangent vector as a point of B^d. For `||x|| > 1` the `mobius_add(-x, y)` denominator and the `(1 - c*||x||^2) * y` numerator make the Möbius difference exceed unit norm for essentially every code; `log_at`/`poincare_distance` then clamp the `atanh` argument at `1 - ARTANH_EPS = 1 - 1e-7` (model/frechet_poincare.py:97-98) and return the same saturated value 2*atanh(1-1e-7) = 16.118 for every slot. All 256 distances tie, `torch.argmin` returns 0, so every item is assigned to code 0 at initialisation. The residual handed to the next level is then `x - log_0(c_0)`, a single constant shift for the whole item set, and the next level's KMeans is fitted to that shifted set; `_copy_init_embed` maps the large-norm centres through `exp_0` (model/layers.py:93), whose norm is `tanh(||v||/2)`, so levels 2 and 3 start with all 256 codes squeezed onto the boundary shell at radius ≈ 0.9999 instead of being spread over the ball. The docstring directly above the call ("Same cost and same residual as the training step: a Euclidean assignment here would start levels 2 and 3 in another geometry than the one the mechanism moves in") is false: the training step maps the latent first, `point = clamp_ball(exp_0(latent))` at model/layers.py:153, and the initialisation does not. This is the curved operation not reaching the computation it claims, at exactly the point where the shared codebook state is created, and it is why the author's own `tests/test_mechanism.py:141-157` ("the start uses the curved cost") passes: it only asserts the returned residual is finite and below 25, which a saturated assignment trivially satisfies.
FINDING REPRODUCTION: By hand, with c = 1 and a collinear worst case: x = 5e, y = r*e, r = 0.5 gives numerator = -(1 + 10r + r^2)*5*e - (1 - 25)*r*e = -43.25e and denominator = 1 + 10r + 25r^2 = 12.25, so `mobius_add(-x, y)` has norm 3.53 > 1 and the distance is the clamped 16.118; the same holds for r = 0.9 (norm 2.50), r = 0.1 (norm 1.58) and r = 0.001 (norm 5.02), and it already saturated at ||x|| = 1.1. Since the residual is `x - log_0(c_0)` with `||log_0(c_0)|| <= 2*atanh(1-1e-4) ~ 18.4`, the shift does not bring it back inside the ball. In code: build the model as `tests/test_mechanism.build()` does, then `x = model.encoder(embeddings)`, `codes = layer.get_code_embs()`, `torch.argmin(layer.frechet.distances(x, codes), -1)` is all zeros and `layer.frechet.distances(x, codes)[0]` is the constant 16.118 for every slot; after `model.init_codebook(embeddings)`, `layer2.get_code_embs().norm(dim=-1).min()` is ≈ 0.9999. The author's suite passes because no test compares the initialisation assignment against the training assignment on the same residual.
FINDING CORRECTION: Feed the ball point, not the tangent vector, in `VQLayer.init_codebook`: `with torch.no_grad(): point = clamp_ball(exp_0(x)); embed_ind = torch.argmin(self.frechet.distances(point, self.get_code_embs()), -1)`, and return `x - log_0(self.embed_code(embed_ind))` as now, so the level-1 residual chain is built from the same geometry the training step uses. (With `use_curvature=False`, `distances` is already the Euclidean cost on the tangent, so that branch needs no change — but the two branches must then be selected for the same reason the step selects them.) Add an assertion that at initialisation not all `embed_ind` are equal and that the level-2/3 codebook radius is not concentrated at the boundary.

FINDING SEVERITY: minor
FINDING LOCATION: model/frechet_poincare.py:131-141 with train_rqvae.py:455-457
FINDING DETAIL: The successor weights are normalised by the batch mean inside `weight_of`, i.e. per rank, while the per-slot mean is formed after the cross-rank all_reduce. Each item therefore enters the reduced weighted mean with `w_i / c_r` where `c_r` is its own rank's batch mean instead of the mean over the whole 4096-item step, so the estimator computed by the four-rank branch is not the estimator the single-process branch computes for the same global batch. It is small (the per-rank means of a 1024-item sample concentrate on the global mean) and it does not remove the coupling, but the two branches do not compute the same quantity, which is exactly what the single-process check is supposed to guarantee.
FINDING REPRODUCTION: In `FrechetCodebook.weight_of`, `weights / weights.mean()` on `item_ids = [0, 1]` with table `[1, 2, ...]` yields `[0.667, 1.333]`; the same two items plus one more item with weight 20 yields `[0.043, 0.087, 0.87]`. Reduce the two batches' `tangent_sum`/`weight_sum` as the trainer does and the slot mean differs although the item set is the same as a single 3-item batch.
FINDING CORRECTION: Normalise by a fixed constant carried with the table — the mean of `item_weights` over the items with support, computed once in `_build_successor_attraction` and stored on the module — instead of by `weights.mean()` of the current batch; then the per-rank sums are additive and the cross-rank reduction reproduces the single-process weighted mean exactly.
